THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimants are in appeal challenging the exoneration of liability on the Insurer and also seeking for enhancement.

2. The Tribunal has exonerated the Insurer on the ground that the Insurance policy which was prevailing as on the date of the accident was not produced and the policy which was produced only indicated that the vehicle was insured from 29.04.2015.
Along with this appeal, a xerox copy of the policy has been produced which indicates that there was a policy in force from 21.10.2014 to 20.10.2015.
Since the accident has occurred on 23.04.2015, it is obvious that the offending vehicle was covered with an insurance policy.

In this view of the matter, the exoneration of the Insurer from the liability cannot be sustained and the same is set aside and it is held that the Insurer of the offending goods vehicle is liable to satisfy the compensation.

3. As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded the following sums as compensation:

4.

In arriving at the compensation towards loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly notional income of the claimant at Rs.6,000/- and has deducted 1/3rd of the same towards personal expenses of the deceased, as he was survived by his wife and a daughter.

5. In cases where there is no evidence to determine the actual income, it is appropriate to adopt the notional income as assessed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which for the year 2015 would be Rs.9,000/-.
6. Out of the said sum, 1/3rd of the same (Rs.3,000/-) would have to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.
The net income will be Rs.6,000/-.

7. As the deceased was aged 64 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121,
the multiplier of '7' would have to be applied.

towards "loss of dependency".
9.

The claimants being the wife and a daughter of the deceased, each of them would be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of love and affection" i.e., in all Rs.88,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".

Further, the claimants would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.97,475/- that had been awarded by the Tribunal towards medical expenses.

11. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums :
Compensation Sl.
As awarded by No. Nature of Heads this Court (In Rs.)

1. Loss of Dependency 5,04,000/-
(Rs.6,000/- x 12 x '7')
2. Loss of love and affection 88,000/-
3. Conventional heads 33,000/-
4. Medical expenses 97,475/-
 Total 7,22,475/-
12.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation of Rs.7,22,475/- as against Rs.5,68,475/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
13. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
14. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded along with interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
